title: FACIL: Flexible DRAM Address Mapping for SoC-PIM Cooperative On-device LLM Inference
problem: On-device LLM inference requires the same model weights to be accessed by both DRAM-based PIM units (for GEMV in the memory-bound decode phase) and SoC processors (for GEMM in the compute-bound prefill phase), but PIM-operable tensor layouts require different DRAM bank mappings from those preferred by SoC processors, creating costly re-layout overheads when switching between the two.
motivation: Edge devices have limited memory capacity, so PIM must function as both a compute unit and a conventional memory device; enabling re-layout-free cooperative inference between SoC and PIM is essential to minimize time-to-first-token on resource-constrained edge hardware.
method: FACIL modifies the memory controller to support different DRAM address mappings for different huge pages (large memory regions), so different mappings can convert the same address to different physical bank locations. Software chooses which mapping to use for each tensor, placing weights where both PIM (processing-in-memory hardware that does fast matrix-vector operations) and SoC processors (which do larger matrix-matrix computations) can access them. The same physical weights work for both types of operations without copying or reorganizing the data, eliminating the costly re-layout overhead when switching between the two.
key_novelty: By using per-huge-page configurable DRAM address mapping in the memory controller, FACIL enables both PIM (processing-in-memory hardware) and SoC (system-on-chip) processors to access model weights from the same banks without data reorganization.
contributions: FACIL: flexible DRAM address mapping that enables simultaneous PIM-operable and SoC-contiguous tensor placement
Memory controller extension assigning different DRAM address mappings to page offset bits per huge page
User-level library for determining and managing appropriate DRAM address mappings at tensor granularity
2.37x and 2.63x time-to-first-token reduction for short conversation and code autocompletion tasks over SoC-PIM baseline

metrics.speedup: 2.37x TTFT reduction (short conversation), 2.63x TTFT reduction (code autocompletion) over SoC-PIM baseline

limitations: The approach is evaluated on edge LLM scenarios with LPDDR-interfaced PIM; applicability to server-class PIM systems with different DRAM packaging is not discussed.
primary_theme: flexible DRAM address mapping for cooperative SoC-PIM LLM inference
